title: Define decision ledger & micro-acceptance steps for Structured Output PRD
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: This ticket establishes a lightweight 'decision ledger' and a set of micro-acceptance steps to coordinate PRD review and sign-off across Engineering, Design, and Legal for the Structured Output V3 initiative. The goal is to replace ad-hoc signoffs with concrete, testable acceptance gates so rollouts (canary/A-B) and rollback criteria are clear to all stakeholders.

Context: The Structured Output PRD introduces a new structured JSON schema for model responses, a versioning contract for model variants, and a partial rollforward path that depends on runtime batching and schema validation hooks. There are multiple cross-team questions outstanding: legal data labeling language, design edge-case handling for nested arrays, and runtime behaviour for partial schema failures. Prior attempts at a single big-signoff caused delays; this ticket defines micro-checkpoints to unblock parallel work.

Scope clarifications and trade-offs:
- We will scope initial rollout to text-generation endpoints only (no embeddings).
- For schema validation failures, runtime will expose a soft-fail mode initially (logs + telemetry) and a hard-fail fallback only after acceptance criteria for fallback behaviour are met. This trades immediate strict correctness for staged reliability validation.
- Legal asked for a short contract clause for telemetry that references the telemetry dashboard; engineering will surface telemetry fields and retention window instead of embedding legal text in technical schema.

Deliverables:
- Decision ledger (single source of truth) documenting each acceptance gate, owner, required artifact, and expected outcome.
- Micro-acceptance checklist for each gate with pass/fail signals.
- Shared Confluence page and assigned reviewers per gate.
- Implementation tasks split into canary controls, telemetry dashboards, design QA checklist, and legal contract snippet.

Risks:
- If telemetry instrumentation is late, Legal cannot approve retention terms and rollout may be delayed.
- Runtime partial-failure behaviour may cause increased error rates for latency-sensitive routes; require a mitigation plan in the engineering gate.

Next steps:
1) Product to publish the decision ledger draft (this ticket).
2) Engineering to provide telemetry event list + initial implementation PR for canary controls.
3) Design to publish QA checklist and representative edge-case mocks.
4) Legal to draft one-paragraph telemetry wording and confirm no additional data residency controls are required.

Notes on collaboration: Links to artifacts are below. Please add comments directly to the decision ledger when you change an acceptance criterion — we intend to use the ledger as the canonical record for signoff and audit.

Acceptance criteria are enumerated and must be marked "Accepted" on the ledger by the named owner to advance the release pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Gate 1 - Schema contract: Design and Engineering agree on JSON schema and 5 representative edge-case examples; Design QA checklist published. (Owner: Rina Gomez)
Gate 2 - Telemetry & Retention: Engineering publishes telemetry event list and dashboard; Legal confirms retention window and wording. (Owners: Eli Thompson, Carlos Mendes)
Gate 3 - Runtime fallback: Canary implementation for soft-fail mode deployed to staging with metrics observed for 48 hours and error budget within threshold. (Owner: Eli Thompson)
Gate 4 - Documentation & SDK: SDK team publishes code samples and compatibility notes; API docs reviewed by PM and Design. (Owners: Omar Patel, Rina Gomez)
Gate 5 - Legal signoff: One-paragraph telemetry clause accepted and no outstanding data residency blockers. (Owner: Carlos Mendes)
